To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a two-dimensional fractionation scheme for serum or plasma proteins results in increased depth and breadth of analysis of the intact protein proteome.

extensive fractionation of serum and plasma by orthogonal two-dimensional chromatography results in identification of a large number of unique proteins and protein isoforms with a high level of confidence.
extensive protein fractionation of serum and plasma is an effective means to increase depth of analysis and to identify protein isoforms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an analytical platform that is suitable for the identification of low-abundance protein markers of disease.
developing and implementing an integrated system for in-depth analysis of serum and plasma proteins.
the identification of proteins in serum and plasma by mass spectrometric methods and the development of strategies for the detection of protein isoforms in these biological fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
extensive protein fractionation of serum or plasma samples results in increased depth and breadth of analysis.
the contribution of protein fractionation is substantial to depth of analysis, but not as much as one would have expected.

the use of fractionation in conjunction with shotgun LC-MS analysis can be used for the identification of proteins in serum and plasma, and this approach is complementary to the use of 2-D gel electrophoresis for the identification of low-abundant proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of two-dimensional fractionation and MS of individual fractions is a robust approach for analysis of the serum proteome and that the IPAS system can be used as a template for other applications.

the depth of analysis of serum and plasma proteome by mass spectrometric analysis is substantially improved by fractionation and that this is achieved at the expense of throughput and sample consumption.
a depth of 2,000 proteins can be reached with a 1 ml sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein fractionation can substantially contribute to depth of analysis in proteomic analysis of serum or plasma.
the depth of analysis of serum and plasma proteome can be increased substantially by combining fractionation and MS analyses of individual fractions.
extensive fractionation of serum proteins prior to mass spectrometry can result in substantial depth of analysis.
